head: Pressure hulls are round.
text: The habitat ring was a flat-sided slab with box lobbies; it is now one continuous rounded hull with bumper tiles over the water jacket. The hub, command module, science section and sample lab have dished ends, and the water tanks have domes in place of cones.

head: Open structure replaces solid beams.
text: The spine is a tube truss with node fittings and the pipe run inside it. The antenna mast, magnetometer boom, tank cradles and nozzle supports are lattice or struts, and the ring's four spokes are braced with stay rods.

head: Radiators are made of panels.
text: Each cold wing is 42 panels on a root manifold, held flat by stay rods from king posts on the spine. Each hot wing is eight carbon segments fed by glowing headers, in place of one solid slab.

head: The drive end has layers.
text: The nozzle coils hang in a strut cone, and the reactor is a vacuum vessel inside its magnet coils inside a cage with beam injectors. The backup fission core sits on the axis between the converter drum and a two-layer shadow shield.

head: Science gear is real hardware.
text: The telescope sits on a fork mount with a baffle, a scarfed hood and a cryoradiator, beside a sunshade of four membranes on a tube frame. The radar is tiles on a back frame, each kind of probe has its own shape on clamp racks, and the launch rail runs through its drive coils with a loader arm.

head: Scale cues added.
text: Handrails, hatches, a docking port, a sample capsule docked at the lab, four suited figures, the name on the ring and hub and the registry UE-16 on the bow. Two glazed roof sectors of the ring show the pink grow lamps of the hydroponics decks.
